On my small plot here in Kilimanjaro, I have been growing beans for many years. The soil is still good because I always put manure from my cows and goats, and beans themselves help the soil by adding nitrogen. I keep my own seed from last season because it has done well and I know it, and with only this small piece of land, my children and I can manage all the work ourselves without hiring anyone. We depend on the rains — the vuli and masika — so I do not irrigate, and I do not buy those expensive chemicals because beans do not need them like coffee does.
